summary: Charles Augustus Kincaid worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He was educated at Sherborne School around 1882 to 1888 and at Balliol College, Oxford, from around 1888 to 1891.

Charles B. Jones works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He completed a PhD at the University of Virginia in 1996 under Paul Groner, and served at the Catholic University of America as Associate Professor and Associate Dean (attested 2016–2019).

Charles Bally was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva and Humboldt University of Berlin, and under Ferdinand de Saussure. He served as Professor of Greek at Collège Calvin (1900–1913) and as Privatdozent at Geneva (1893–1939), succeeding Saussure.
Charles Barbier de Meynard was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Julius Mohl and was attested as a member of the Institut de France in 1894.
Charles Bowles was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Hindustani at Addiscombe Military Seminary from around 1836 to 1861, succeeding John Shakespear.

Charles Bruce worked in Indology after studying at Harrow School, Westminster, Yale, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. His posts included King's College London (unpaid Sanskrit Professor, 1865–1869), the British Museum, Royal College Curepipe, and the UK Government (1878–1904).

Charles Burnett is a historian and philosopher who earned his degrees at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at St John's College, the University of Sheffield, and the Warburg Institute, where he became Professor of Arabic/Islamic Influences in Europe in 1999.
Charles Chapman was an Indologist who studied at Hoxton Academy and under the traditional teacher Mahesha. He was a founder of The Asiatic Society.

Charles Cutler Torrey was a scholar of religious studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics who studied under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900), founded the American Schools of Oriental Research (1901), and was a professor at Yale (1900–1932).

Charles D. Orzech works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, completing his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro (attested 1998–2006) and was a National Humanities Center Fellow (2009–2010).

Charles DiSimone specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD from the University of Munich by 2016. He was affiliated with the University of Munich (attested 2021) and Ghent University (attested 2026).

Charles Duroiselle was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and archaeology. He served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940), Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of India Burma Circle (1919, 1936), and Professor at the University of Rangoon (~1920–1939).

Charles Edmund Godakumbura specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and archaeology, receiving multiple degrees from the University of London. He taught at SOAS (around 1953–1959) and served as Archaeological Commissioner for the Archaeological Survey of India (1956–1967), succeeding Senarath Paranavitana.

Charles Egbert Kennet was a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied at Bishop's College, Calcutta. He served as a teacher (1872) and later Principal (1877) at Madras Theological College, and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.

Charles Eliot worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Cheltenham College and Balliol College, Oxford, he served in the Foreign Office (~1886–1904) and held vice-chancellorships at the University of Sheffield (~1905–1912) and the University of Hong Kong (1912–1918).

Charles Elliott worked in Indology and was educated at Fort William College. He held positions with the East India Company and served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society from around 1837 to 1856.

Charles Evelyn Arbuthnot William Oldham was an Indologist and historian who studied at Balliol College, Oxford. He served as Assistant Editor of the Indian Antiquary (~1925–1931) and Honorary Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1935–1941).

Charles Gabriel Seligman was an ethnologist and historian who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital. He held the chair of Ethnology at the London School of Economics and the University of London from 1913 to 1934.

Charles Georges Marcel Autran was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut Français d'Archéologie Orientale, and later served as a professor at Aix-Marseille University.
Charles Godfrey Chenevix Trench was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his B.A. studies at Lincoln College, University of Oxford, between approximately 1896 and 1900.
